# 1 Chronicles Chapter 10 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 376r–376v

---

**1** The Philistines attacked Israel, and the Israelites fled before them. Many fell dead on Mount Gilboa. **2** The Philistines overtook Saul and his sons, killing Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchi-shua. **3** The fighting raged fiercely around Saul. Enemy archers found him, and he was badly wounded.

**4** Saul told his armor-bearer, "Draw your sword and run me through, before these pagans come and humiliate me." But the armor-bearer was too terrified and refused. So Saul took his own sword and fell on it. **5** When the armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he too fell on his sword and died.

**6** And so Saul perished — he and his three sons — and his entire dynasty came to an end. **7** When the Israelites living in the valley saw that the army had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned their towns and ran. The Philistines moved in and occupied them.

**8** The next day, when the Philistines came to loot the bodies on the battlefield, they found Saul and his sons lying dead on Mount Gilboa. **9** They stripped Saul's body, took his head and his armor, and sent word throughout Philistia, announcing the victory to their idols and their people. **10** They displayed his armor in the temple of their gods and nailed his skull to the wall of Dagon's temple.

**11** When the people of Jabesh-gilead heard everything the Philistines had done to Saul, **12** their bravest warriors went out, retrieved the bodies of Saul and his sons, and brought them back to Jabesh. They buried the bones under the great oak tree there and fasted for seven days.

**13** Saul died because of his unfaithfulness to the LORD. He had disobeyed the LORD's command, and he had even consulted a spirit-medium for guidance. **14** He never sought the LORD's direction. So the LORD took his life and handed the kingdom over to David son of Jesse.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 4 — "uncircumcised":** Saul uses the word as a term of contempt — it marks the Philistines as outside the covenant community. The fear is not just death but desecration by those who stand outside Israel's sacred identity.

**Verse 6 — The Chronicler's erasure:** The phrase "all his house died together" is striking because historically, Saul's son Ish-bosheth ruled briefly after him (2 Samuel 2-4). The Chronicler simply omits this — for him, there is no legitimate transition; David follows Saul directly by divine appointment.

**Verse 13-14 — Two sins, one verdict:** The Chronicler names Saul's offenses precisely: (1) *ma'al* — a term for sacrilege, violating what belongs to God; (2) consulting a medium at Endor (1 Sam 28). Then the devastating conclusion: Saul never sought the LORD. The Hebrew pun — *Sha'ul* (asked/demanded) who failed to *sha'al* (ask) the LORD — reverberates through the passage.

*— PNEUMA*
